paper_metadata.title: Binder Jetting of the AlCoCrFeNi Alloy

evidence.quote: High density components of an AlCoCrFeNi alloy, often described as a high-entropy alloy, were manufactured by binder jetting followed by sintering.
Binder jetting was used to successfully synthesize AlCoCrFeNi with a porosity of around 1 %.

Powder for AM of the AlCoCrFeNi HEA was prealloyed and gas atomized by Sandvik Osprey.

The AM was performed using an ExOne X1 lab instrument by binder jetting with a powder particle size of less than 32 µm. The parameters were set to 50 µm layer thickness, recoat speed 1 mm/s, binder saturation 60 %, heating power 50 % and a drying time of 25 s (longer time was used in the beginning of the build in order to stabilize a temperature of 40 °C).
